2607.21458.title: Detecting LLM-Generated Tokens in Human--LLM Coauthored Text
2607.21458.paper_summary: The rise of human-AI collaborative writing has created a growing need for fine-grained detection methods that support localizing likely LLM-generated content in mixed-authorship documents. Existing methods for detecting LLM-generated text mainly focus on document-level classification and cannot identify which parts of the text are generated by LLMs. This paper introduces a new method to address this urgent need. Our method operates at the token level, the natural unit of modern language models, and builds on existing token-level detection scores. The key idea is to smooth adjacent token scores to reduce their variability, while using an adaptive Lepski-type rule to select the bandwidth according to the local authorship structure. Our method is simple to implement and does not require token-level labeled data for training. Theoretically, we characterize this trade-off and show that the proposed method achieves favorable mean square error performance in estimating the underlying signal. Empirically, we demonstrate strong performance of our method against a wide range of baselines in both synthetic datasets and a realistic dataset. We deploy a publicly accessible website that implements the methods as well.
2607.21458.paper_summary_zh: 人類與人工智慧協作寫作的興起，催生了對精細檢測方法的需求，以支持在混合作者的文件中定位可能由大型語言模型（LLM）生成的內容。現有的檢測LLM生成文本的方法主要集中在文件級別的分類，無法識別文本中哪些部分是由LLM生成的。本文介紹了一種新的方法來應對這一迫切需求。我們的方法在標記層面運作，這是現代語言模型的自然單位，並基於現有的標記級檢測分數。其關鍵思想是平滑相鄰標記的分數，以減少其變異性，同時使用自適應Lepski類型的規則根據當地的作者結構選擇帶寬。我們的方法實現簡單，且不需要標記級別的標註數據進行訓練。在理論上，我們對這一權衡進行了特徵描述，並顯示所提出的方法在估計潛在信號時實現了有利的均方誤差性能。在實證方面，我們展示了我們的方法在合成數據集和現實數據集上對一系列基準的強大表現。我們還部署了一個公開可訪問的網站，實現了這些方法。
